## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Visākhā Sutta* (Ud 8.8, PTS Ud 91) is the eighth discourse of the eighth chapter of the *Udāna* [SuttaCentral]. In this sutta, the prominent lay disciple Lady Visākhā expresses a wish for many grandchildren [SuttaCentral].
Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include the fifth chapter of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (*Priyavarga*, UV 5), its Tibetan translation (*Uv Kg* 5, *Agreeable things*), and two Chinese translations in the Taishō canon: T 212.6 and T 213.5 (*Fa ji yao song jing* chapter 5) [SuttaCentral]. The text is also cited in post-canonical Pali exegetical treatises, specifically the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 1) and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 15) [SuttaCentral].
According to DharmaNexus text-reuse data, the sutta shares 110 matching passages across 20 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest internal Pali parallels occur with the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (particularly AN 8.43, AN 3.70, AN 6.54, AN 10.90, and AN 4.111), the *Kosala Saṁyutta* (SN 3.19), the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Vinaya* (*Cīvarakkhandhaka*, Kd 8), and another *Visākhā Sutta* in the *Udāna* (Ud 2.9) [DharmaNexus]. In agreement with SuttaCentral's reference to the *Nettippakaraṇa*, DharmaNexus demonstrates a direct, identical text reuse with the *Otaraṇahāravibhaṅga* (Ne 15 §6.1–8.4, similarity 1.0) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language automated alignments also detect shared passages with a Tibetan canonical text (BO_K01_D0005_H0005) and the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus]. None of the secondary literature passages in the dossier directly discuss Ud 8.8, referring instead to other canonical discourses or commentarial narratives concerning Lady Visākhā or the male disciple Visākha.
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
